svg.title: koda cost per run on read-only and general questions
svg.desc: Horizontal bar chart. Median cost per run on read-only and general questions (tasks e1 and f1, 10 runs per tool, all answers correct), one-shot runs each in a new directory, DeepSeek list price, peak basis: koda $0.0015, opencode $0.0031 (2.5 times koda, paired, koda lower in 10/10 rounds), Hermes Agent $0.0050 (4.6 times, koda lower in 10/10 rounds). Condition: the new directory per run kept opencode's and Hermes' prompts out of the cache; with every input token cached the paired ratios would be 0.90x / 1.15x, so koda would not be cheaper than opencode; on edit tasks opencode is cheaper. Run main-20260930, 2026-09-30, deepseek-flash. Full results (incl. where koda trails): benchmarks/
svg.text: read-only and general questions
One-shot runs, each in a new directory: about
half of opencode's cost, under a third of Hermes'.

for all three · same model, deepseek-flash

path.title: Hermes Agent: median $0.0050 per run (n=10); IQR $0.003987–$0.006658

svg.text: 4.6× koda's cost, paired · koda lower in 10/10 rounds
Bars on one scale from $0 · bar = median of 10 runs · line =
middle 50% of runs (IQR)
CONDITION
Each run in a new, randomly named directory
kept opencode's and Hermes' prompts out of the
cache (their system prompts carry per-run
content, likely the path; koda's prompt has no
path). With everything cached koda is not
cheaper than opencode. On edits opencode is
cheaper.
Paired ratio vs opencode / Hermes: as measured 2.5× /
4.6× · with no cache at all 1.6× / 3.6× · with every
input token cached 0.90× / 1.15×. The cache split is
inferred from prompt lengths and cache counts; request
bodies were not logged.
deepseek-flash for all three tools, one API account · koda
0.1.0 @ 63fda57 · opencode 1.18.33 · Hermes Agent
Cost = DeepSeek list price, peak basis (per 1M tokens:
cache hit $0.006, miss $0.30, output $1.20); the runs were
off-peak and billed at 50% · paired = median of the 10
same-round tool ÷ koda ratios
